General_Description.Text: FRUIT is a SeeDB-derived optical clearing method that utilizes a cocktail of fructose and urea. This combination exerts a synergistic effect on tissue transparency, achieving greater tissue transparency and requiring shorter clearing time than either fructose or urea alone. The final FRUIT solution has a low viscosity, enabling the transparency of the whole adult rabbit brain via arterial perfusion, which is not possible with saturated fructose solution. FRUIT maintains good compatibility with enhanced yellow fluorescent protein and preserves the fluorescence of the lipophilic tracer DiI. It provides a volume-independent optical clearing method retaining the advantages of SeeDB, particularly compatibility with lipophilic tracers.
Text_Reference: Abstract: 'Here we report a SeeDB-derived optical clearing method, termed FRUIT, which utilizes a cocktail of fructose and urea. As demonstrated in the adult mouse brain, combination of these two highly water-soluble clearing agents exerts a synergistic effect on clearance. More importantly, the final FRUIT solution has low viscosity so as to produce transparency of the whole adult rabbit brain via arterial perfusion, which is impossible to achieve with a saturated fructose solution. In addition to good compatibility with enhanced yellow fluorescent protein, the cocktail also preserves the fluorescence of the lipophilic tracer DiI.'

Introduction: 'Here we report an optical clearing method that uses a gradient of cocktail solutions, termed FRUIT, which is mainly composed of fructose and urea in variable proportions. FRUIT achieved greater tissue transparency and required a shorter clearing time than either fructose or urea alone. Urea-mediated tissue expansion could be controlled by increasing the concentration of fructose in the initial cocktail solution. Importantly, the presence of urea reduced the need for fructose. As compared with the highest concentration of SeeDB, the dynamic viscosity of the final FRUIT cocktail was lowered by over 97% so as to render the whole adult rabbit brain transparent via arterial perfusion. Under two-photon microscopy, the fluorescence of both enhanced yellow fluorescent protein (eYFP) and DiI was well preserved in the FRUIT-processed brain. The present study provides a new cocktail recipe which underlies a volume-independent and lipophilic tracer-compatible optical tissue clearing method.'

Discussion: 'By means of arterial perfusion, FRUIT can achieve tissue clearance independent of brain volume limitations. Although CUBIC (Susaki et al., 2014) and a modified version of CLARITY (Yang et al., 2014) are also scalable clearing methods, both of them render the whole mammalian brain transparent by removing hydrophobic lipids, which makes it impossible to clear DiI-labeled brain samples. Thus, FRUIT represents a distinctive clearing method which is both independent of brain volume and compatible with lipophilic tracers.'

Tissue_Types.Text1: The FRUIT method produces transparency of the whole adult rabbit brain via arterial perfusion, which is impossible to achieve with a saturated fructose solution.
Text1_Reference: INTRODUCTION section: 'More importantly, the final FRUIT solution has low viscosity so as to produce transparency of the whole adult rabbit brain via arterial perfusion, which is impossible to achieve with a saturated fructose solution.'

Time_Consumption.Text1: The total time required for FRUIT (35:100) to clear adult mouse brains was as short as 2.5 days, a reduction of approximately 40% as compared with SeeDB.
Text1_Reference: RESULTS section: 'Dynamic viscosity measurements revealed that whether at room temperature (i.e., 29°C) or under mild heating conditions (i.e., 37°C), 100% FRUIT was 30 times less viscous than a 130% fructose solution (Figure 5A). Low viscosity not only improved permeability but also accelerated clearance as evidenced by the fact that the total time required for FRUIT (35:100) to clear adult mouse brains was as short as 2.5 days, a reduction of approximately 40% as compared with SeeDB (Figure 3A).'

Time_Consumption.Text2: FRUIT protocol was established as follows: 8 h each in 35, 40, and 60%(wt/vol) FRUIT, 12 h in 80% (wt/vol) FRUIT and 24 h in 100% (wt/vol) FRUIT.
Text2_Reference: MATERIALS AND METHODS section: 'In order to achieve maximal transparency without deformation, the optimal FRUIT protocol was established as follows: 8 h each in 35, 40, and 60%(wt/vol) FRUIT, 12 h in 80% (wt/vol) FRUIT and 24 h in 100% (wt/vol) FRUIT. Incubation at a temperature over 37°C is not recommended due to concern regarding the breakdown of FRUIT. Samples could be stored in 100% (wt/vol) FRUIT over 2 months at 4°C.'

Time_Consumption.Text3: The best tissue clearance by the 100% FRUIT solution was achieved after 24 h and maintained thereafter, suggesting that a 24 h incubation was sufficient for 100% FRUIT to achieve optimal clearance of PFA-fixed adult mouse hemi-brains.
Text3_Reference: RESULTS section: 'Moreover, the best tissue clearance by the 100% FRUIT solution was achieved after 24 h and maintained thereafter (Figure 3G), suggesting that a 24 h incubation was sufficient for 100% FRUIT to achieve optimal clearance of PFA-fixed adult mouse hemi-brains.'

Tissue_Deformation.Text1: The final volume of brain samples increased after treatment with FRUIT (20:115), indicating tissue expansion.
Text1_Reference: RESULTS section, 'CONTROLLABLE TISSUE DEFORMATION BY THE COCKTAIL': 'We noted that the final volume of brain samples also increased after treatment with FRUIT (20:115).'

Tissue_Deformation.Text2: The brain stopped expanding at a FRUIT concentration of 40%, after which it partially recovered, indicating that the better tissue transparency observed with FRUIT treatment was unlikely to be mainly mediated by tissue expansion.
Text2_Reference: RESULTS section, 'CONTROLLABLE TISSUE DEFORMATION BY THE COCKTAIL': 'We therefore, examined this possibility, and found that the brain stopped expanding at a FRUIT concentration of 40%, after which it partially recovered.'

Tissue_Deformation.Text3: Only 35% FRUIT was able to preserve the original size of the brain, whereas a lower or higher concentration caused expansion or shrinkage, respectively.
Text3_Reference: RESULTS section, 'CONTROLLABLE TISSUE DEFORMATION BY THE COCKTAIL': 'It was found that only 35% FRUIT was able to preserve the original size of the brain, whereas a lower or higher concentration caused expansion or shrinkage, respectively.'

Tissue_Deformation.Text4: A gradient of FRUIT solutions starting from 35% preserved the brain size well, whereas those with a lower or higher start concentration deformed the brain.
Text4_Reference: RESULTS section, 'CONTROLLABLE TISSUE DEFORMATION BY THE COCKTAIL': 'As expected, a gradient of FRUIT solutions starting from 35% preserved the brain size well, whereas those with a lower or higher start concentration deformed the brain.'

Tissue_Deformation.Text5: 0.5 × PBS in 20–80% FRUIT solutions was sufficient to control expansion of the brain.
Text5_Reference: RESULTS section, 'CONTROLLABLE TISSUE DEFORMATION BY THE COCKTAIL': 'This revealed that 0.5 × PBS in 20–80% FRUIT solutions was sufficient to control for expansion of the brain.'

Tissue_Deformation.Text6: The FRUIT procedure beginning at a concentration of 35% rendered the brain clearer than that using 0.5 × PBS as a solvent, a gradient comprising 35, 40, 60, 80, and 100% FRUIT solutions, was finally selected as the optimal approach. However, it should be noted that the optimal procedure might vary depending on animal age, tissue volume, fixation time, solution temperature and other factors.
Text6_Reference: RESULTS section, 'CONTROLLABLE TISSUE DEFORMATION BY THE COCKTAIL': 'After finding that the FRUIT procedure beginning at a concentration of 35% rendered the brain clearer than that using 0.5 × PBS as a solvent (Figure 3H), a gradient comprising 35, 40, 60, 80, and 100% FRUIT solutions (see Figure 3A), was finally selected as the optimal approach. However, it should be noted that the optimal procedure might vary depending on animal age, tissue volume, fixation time, solution temperature and other factors.'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text1: Under two-photon microscopy, the fluorescence of both enhanced yellow fluorescent protein (eYFP) and DiI was well preserved in the FRUIT-processed brain.
Text1_Reference: INTRODUCTION section: 'In addition to good compatibility with enhanced yellow fluorescent protein, the cocktail also preserves the fluorescence of the lipophilic tracer DiI.'
RESULTS section: 'Under two-photon microscopy, the fluorescence of both enhanced yellow fluorescent protein (eYFP) and DiI was well preserved in the FRUIT-processed brain.'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text2: The fluorescence of cytosolic eYFP in the brains of Thy1-eYFP (line H) transgenic mice was well preserved after FRUIT treatment, similar to the result obtained after SeeDB treatment.
Text2_Reference: RESULTS section, 'SCALABLE CLEARANCE WITH eYFP AND DiI COMPATIBILITY': 'The fluorescence of cytosolic eYFP in the brains of Thy1-eYFP (line H) transgenic mice was well preserved after FRUIT treatment, similar to the result obtained after SeeDB treatment.'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text3: FRUIT could also clear brains labeled with the lipophilic dye DiI, implying that the plasma membrane of FRUIT-processed brains remains intact.
Text3_Reference: RESULTS section, 'SCALABLE CLEARANCE WITH eYFP AND DiI COMPATIBILITY': 'FRUIT could also clear brains labeled with the lipophilic dye DiI, implying that the plasma membrane of FRUIT-processed brains remains intact.'

Preservation_Stability.Text1: Samples could be stored in 100% (wt/vol) FRUIT over 2 months at 4°C.
Text1_Reference: MATERIALS AND METHODS section, OPTICAL CLEARING USING FRUIT subheading: 'Samples could be stored in 100% (wt/vol) FRUIT over 2 months at 4°C.'

Preservation_Stability.Text2: Although Scale-treated samples are very fragile, FRUIT-treated samples did not display noticeable fragility.
Text2_Reference: RESULTS section: 'Although Scale-treated samples are very fragile (Hama et al., 2011), FRUIT-treated samples did not display noticeable fragility.'

Application.Text1: FRUIT achieves transparency of the whole adult rabbit brain via arterial perfusion, which is impossible to achieve with a saturated fructose solution.
Text1_Reference: INTRODUCTION section: 'More importantly, the final FRUIT solution has low viscosity so as to produce transparency of the whole adult rabbit brain via arterial perfusion, which is impossible to achieve with a saturated fructose solution.'

MATERIALS AND METHODS section, 'PERFUSION-ASSISTED CLEARING USING FRUIT': 'Perfusion of FRUIT solutions rendered the whole brain transparent whereas 130% SeeDB was too viscous to be arterially perfused.'

Application.Text2: FRUIT preserves the fluorescence of the lipophilic tracer DiI, making it suitable for tract tracing of post-fixed whole brains.
Text2_Reference: INTRODUCTION section: 'In addition to good compatibility with enhanced yellow fluorescent protein, the cocktail also preserves the fluorescence of the lipophilic tracer DiI.'

RESULTS section, 'SCALABLE CLEARANCE WITH eYFP AND DiI COMPATIBILITY': 'Interestingly, and also similar to SeeDB, FRUIT could also clear brains labeled with the lipophilic dye DiI, implying that the plasma membrane of FRUIT-processed brains remains intact and that FRUIT is suitable for tract tracing of post-fixed whole brains.'

Application.Text3: FRUIT is compatible with enhanced yellow fluorescent protein (eYFP), preserving its fluorescence in cleared brain samples.
Text3_Reference: RESULTS section, 'SCALABLE CLEARANCE WITH eYFP AND DiI COMPATIBILITY': 'The fluorescence of cytosolic eYFP in the brains of Thy1-eYFP (line H) transgenic mice was well preserved after FRUIT treatment, similar to the result obtained after SeeDB treatment.'

Application.Text4: We envision that FRUIT could even be applicable to the optical clearing of primate brains.
Text4_Reference: DISCUSSION section: 'As perfusion-assisted release of clearing agents is not restricted by organ volume (Yang et al., 2014), we envision that FRUIT could even be applicable to the optical clearing of primate brains.'

Application.Text5: By means of arterial perfusion, FRUIT can achieve tissue clearance independent of brain volume limitations.
Text5_Reference: DISCUSSION section: 'By means of arterial perfusion, FRUIT can achieve tissue clearance independent of brain volume limitations.'

Note.Text1: The viscosity of saturated fructose solution (e.g., 130% wt/vol at 37°C) is extremely high, which limits its ability to permeate into brain samples as well as making solution preparation and manipulation difficult.
Text1_Reference: INTRODUCTION section: 'However, the viscosity of saturated fructose (e.g., 130% wt/vol at 37°C) is extremely high, which limits its ability to permeate into brain samples as well as making solution preparation and manipulation difficult.'

Note.Text2: Although incubation at a higher temperature could improve permeability and fluidity issues, this would cause partial quenching of fluorescent proteins.
Text2_Reference: INTRODUCTION section: 'Although incubation at a higher temperature could improve these permeability and fluidity issues, this would cause partial quenching of fluorescent proteins.'

Note.Text3: Extremely high viscosity prohibits application of SeeDB via arterial perfusion.
Text3_Reference: INTRODUCTION section: 'Arterial perfusion-assisted delivery is also efficient for rapid diffusion of clearing agents across the whole brain (Yang et al., 2014), but extremely high viscosity prohibits application of SeeDB via arterial perfusion.'

Note.Text4: The final FRUIT solution has low viscosity so as to produce transparency of the whole adult rabbit brain via arterial perfusion, which is impossible to achieve with a saturated fructose solution.

Note.Text6: The combination of fructose and urea exerted a synergistic effect on clearance competence.
Text6_Reference: RESULTS section, 'Synergistically improved clearing competence of the cocktail': 'However, both the Scale A2 solution and a descending gradient of urea solutions produced only negligible transmittance within a similar incubation period (Figures 3E, F), suggesting that the combination of fructose and urea exerted a synergistic rather than an additive effect on clearance competence.'

Note.Text7: FRUIT-processed tissues already displayed considerable transmittance at the initial concentration (i.e., 20%) and continued to improve until 100%.
Text7_Reference: RESULTS section, 'Synergistically improved clearing competence of the cocktail': 'In contrast, FRUIT-processed tissues already displayed considerable transmittance at the initial concentration (i.e., 20%) and continued to improve until 100%.'

Note.Text8: FRUIT-mediated tissue expansion was mainly due to the high concentration of urea.
Text8_Reference: RESULTS section, 'Controllable tissue deformation by the cocktail': 'By comparing FRUIT with SeeDB and Scale, we concluded that FRUIT-mediated tissue expansion was mainly due to the high concentration of urea.'

Note.Text9: FRUIT-treated samples did not display noticeable fragility.
Text9_Reference: RESULTS section, 'Scalable clearance with eYFP and DiI compatibility': 'Although Scale-treated samples are very fragile (Hama et al., 2011), FRUIT-treated samples did not display noticeable fragility.'

Note.Text10: FRUIT could also clear brains labeled with the lipophilic dye DiI, implying that the plasma membrane of FRUIT-processed brains remains intact.
Text10_Reference: RESULTS section, 'Scalable clearance with eYFP and DiI compatibility': 'Interestingly, and also similar to SeeDB (Ke et al., 2013), FRUIT could also clear brains labeled with the lipophilic dye DiI (Figures 6E,F), implying that the plasma membrane of FRUIT-processed brains remains intact and that FRUIT is suitable for tract tracing of post-fixed whole brains.'

Note.Text11: FRUIT would not facilitate immunostaining of the whole brain.
Text11_Reference: DISCUSSION section:'However, SeeDB and our method would not facilitate immunostaining of the whole brain (Chung et al., 2013; Renier et al., 2014; Susaki et al., 2014; Tainaka et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2014), because they are not intentionally designed to remove lipids which render tissue poorly accessible to molecular probes, such as antibodies.'
